name: Webpage
description: Turns a webpage's HTML into readable native content: headings, paragraphs, images, and links as typed blocks.

operations.name: page.blocks
operations.description: Extracts a page's readable content from its HTML as typed blocks in document order, with navigation chrome, scripts, and forms stripped and relative urls resolved.

inputs.name: html
inputs.description: The page's HTML, from http.get's "body" output

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The page's own url, so relative links and images resolve

outputs.name: blocks
outputs.description: Content rows: kind is heading | paragraph | item | quote | code | image | link; headings carry level 1-3; images carry src; links (and linked headings) carry href

operations.howto: Webpage reader pattern: route http.get's "body" output to a state key, bind "html" from that key and "url" from the same link the fetch used, and route "blocks" to a state key a list element binds its items from. The list template holds one child per kind, each gated by visibleWhen on {"source": "item", "sourceId": "kind", "operator": "equals", "value": "heading"} (and paragraph, item, quote, code, image, link): text elements for the text kinds (bind content from item.text; give headings a large size knob), an image element binding src from item.src, and for link rows a button binding content from item.text. Give that link button click bindings that chain http.get with url from {"source": "item", "sourceId": "href"} and then page.blocks again: clicking a shown link then opens that page in place, which makes the app a native browser of readable pages. Two http.get operations are normal: one bound to the url input, one bound to item.href.
